title: How to Organize the Space Under Your Sink So It Stays That Way
description: A simple zoning system for cleaning supplies, spare items and plumbing access without turning the cabinet into a pile you have to empty.
body_html:
The cabinet under a sink has an awkward shape, pipes in the middle and a habit of becoming a storage graveyard. The trick is to organize around access rather than trying to fill every centimetre.

Create three zones

Keep everyday supplies in the easiest-to-reach area, backup supplies farther back, and leave a clear zone around plumbing connections. Anything that blocks a shutoff valve or trap is in the wrong place.

Use removable containers

Small bins or trays make it possible to lift a group of items out at once. Choose containers that tolerate the environment and do not require permanent installation if the cabinet may need plumbing work.

Store by task

Instead of grouping every product by brand or size, group related tasks: surface cleaning, laundry, spare toiletries or maintenance. This makes the cabinet easier to use when you are in a hurry.

Leave a leak-detection zone

Do not cover the cabinet floor with absorbent clutter. A clear, visible area makes drips easier to notice before a small plumbing problem becomes hidden damage.

Do a five-minute reset monthly

  • Remove empty products.
  • Check for leaks or dampness.
  • Return items to their zones.
  • Move backups out of the prime-access area.
  • Keep plumbing shutoffs reachable.

The best storage system is not the one that holds the most. It is the one that makes the next task easier.
